newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian cabinet approves draft banking law.
newsitem.headline: Italian cabinet approves draft banking law.

text.p: The Italian cabinet approved a draft delegate law on Thursday on restructuring the banking sector and the nonprofit-making foundations which control a host of Italy's banks, a statement from the Prime Minister's office said.

The draft law aims to draw a distinction between charitable foundations and the actual banks, make the entrance of private capital into the banks easier, loosen the foundations' grip on the sector and turn the latter into private nonprofit-making companies.

Although the government has privatised some Italian banks in recent years, many banks remain under the control of charitable foundations which are themselves often directly or indirectly controlled by local and national state bodies.

The draft law also aims to encourage reorganisation and concentration in the bank sector. Analysts say restructuring and rationalisation are needed for Italian banks which are underperforming and overstaffed compared to their European competitors.
The statement said the draft law gave the government power for 90 days to reorganise the tax and legislative framework of the foundations and to carry out tax changes in the bank sector.

It said foundations selling their stakes in banks would have a three year tax exemption on capital gains from the sales while from the fourth to the seventh year after the law is enacted tax charges would be halved.

Further details were not given but a previous draft examined by the cabinet allowed foundations to convert ordinary shares they own in banks into savings or privileged shares, meaning control could pass to private shareholders leaving foundations with a portfolio investment.
The draft approved on Thursday now has to be approved by parliament. Under a delegate law, parliament gives the government a free hand to draft legislation within preset limits.
